pool.question: A project forecast shows a 9% cost overrun against a board tolerance of ±5%. What should the project manager do?
options: Raise an exception report to the board with options and a recommendation
Stop the project without consulting anyone
Absorb it quietly and hope to recover
pool.explanation: Breaching tolerance triggers escalation with options; the PM does not have authority to accept it alone or change tolerances.

pool.question: Which factors most strongly favour an agile lifecycle? (Select all that apply.)
options: Customers are available for frequent feedback
Late changes are extremely costly, as in poured concrete structures
Small usable increments can be delivered and tested with users
pool.explanation: Evolving requirements, incremental delivery and available feedback favour agile; high late-change cost favours predictive.

pool.question: Mid-project, a competitor launches a product that makes your project's main benefit unlikely. What should governance do at the next gate?
options: Continue as planned because the budget is approved
Reassess the business case and consider changing direction or stopping
Increase the budget to speed up
pool.explanation: Gates exist to test continued viability; stopping or pivoting can be the right decision.

pool.question: Which is a well-defined benefit?
options: Reduce median claims processing time from 10 to 4 working days by Q3, owned by the claims operations manager
pool.explanation: It is measurable, time-bound, has a baseline and an owner; the others are vague or are outputs.

pool.question: A steering committee has 15 members, meets monthly and rarely decides anything. Which changes most improve governance? (Select all that apply.)
options: Set tolerances and manage by exception
Reduce membership to those with decision authority and essential perspectives
Add a longer status presentation to each meeting
Clarify who holds the decision right for major choices
pool.explanation: Smaller boards, tolerances and clear decision rights speed decisions; longer status decks do not.

pool.question: In the five-case model, which case asks whether the project is affordable and fundable?
pool.explanation: The financial case covers affordability and funding; the economic case covers value for money across options.

pool.question: A project has delivered a new CRM, but sales staff keep using spreadsheets. What has not yet been achieved?
options: The outcome of changed behaviour, and so the benefits
pool.explanation: Outputs enable outcomes; benefits depend on people actually changing how they work.

pool.question: O = 6, M = 9, P = 18 days. What is the PERT expected duration?
A RACI shows two people as Accountable for go-live approval. What is the risk and fix?
options: Unclear accountability; assign exactly one Accountable role
No risk; more accountability is better
pool.explanation: Multiple A's diffuse ownership; one A per decision is the rule.

pool.question: Which are good practices for requirements? (Select all that apply.)
options: Include non-functional requirements such as security and performance
Mark every requirement as Must have
Trace requirements to design and test cases
pool.explanation: Testability, non-functional coverage and traceability are key; marking everything Must removes flexibility.

pool.question: A team's last 8 sprints delivered 18–26 points. 210 points remain; the sponsor wants a single date. What is the best response?
options: Double the team size to guarantee 5 sprints
Present a range of about 9 to 12 sprints, explain the uncertainty, and agree a target with a risk buffer
Promise 8 sprints to satisfy the sponsor
pool.explanation: 210/26 ≈ 8.1 (round up to 9) and 210/18 ≈ 11.7 (12). Ranges communicate real uncertainty; adding people rarely scales linearly.

pool.question: When should procurement for an item with a 10-week lead time, needed in week 16, start?
options: No later than week 6, preferably with buffer
pool.explanation: Plan backwards from the need date using the lead time, plus a buffer.

pool.question: Which contract type best suits evolving scope where the buyer can manage the work closely?
options: Time and materials, ideally with a cap and clear reporting
pool.explanation: T&M provides flexibility for evolving scope; caps and reporting control cost.

pool.question: A team's estimates are consistently 30% too low. Which actions address the planning fallacy? (Select all that apply.)
options: Use historical actuals (reference classes) to calibrate
Remove all buffers to create urgency
pool.explanation: Calibration, feedback and reducing pressure improve estimates; removing buffers worsens the problem.

pool.question: Which item belongs in the 'Issues' section of a RAID log?
options: A vendor might go out of business
Users are assumed to be available for UAT
The test environment has been down since Monday
The app depends on a CRM release
pool.explanation: Issues are current problems. The others are a risk, an assumption and a dependency.

pool.question: BAC = 800k, PV = 400k, EV = 320k, AC = 400k. Which statement is correct?
options: EAC = 800k because the budget is fixed

pool.question: A burnup chart shows scope rising from 200 to 260 points while completed work grows steadily. What is the key insight?
options: Scope growth is pushing the completion date out; trade-offs are needed
pool.explanation: Burnups separate scope from progress, making scope growth visible.

pool.question: Defects found by customers rose for three releases. A 5 Whys traces the cause to vague acceptance criteria entering sprints. What is the most effective fix?
options: Require testable acceptance criteria before items enter a sprint and protect refinement time
Hire more testers at the end
Extend the final test phase only
pool.explanation: Prevention upstream beats inspection downstream; the root cause is in refinement, not testing capacity.

pool.question: Which is a threat response that transfers impact to another party?
options: Changing the design to eliminate the risk
pool.explanation: Insurance transfers financial impact; design change avoids, testing mitigates, doing nothing accepts.

pool.question: Which techniques help counter optimism bias and groupthink in risk identification? (Select all that apply.)
pool.explanation: These practices widen input and make it safe to raise problems; a single voice increases bias.

pool.question: Status is green, but the RAID log has 14 issues older than three weeks and several dependencies with no owner on the providing side. What should the PM conclude?
options: Execution health is weaker than reported; address aged issues and unowned dependencies and review status rules
Status is accurate because milestones have not slipped yet
pool.explanation: Aged issues and unowned dependencies are leading indicators of slippage, and rule-based status should reflect them.

pool.question: What is the maximum length of a Sprint?
pool.explanation: The Scrum Guide sets Sprints at one month or less; many teams choose two weeks.

pool.question: Which list correctly pairs Scrum artifacts with their commitments?
options: Product Backlog–Product Goal; Sprint Backlog–Sprint Goal; Increment–Definition of Done
Product Backlog–Definition of Done; Sprint Backlog–Product Goal; Increment–Sprint Goal
Product Backlog–Sprint Goal; Sprint Backlog–Definition of Done; Increment–Product Goal
Sprint Backlog–Release plan; Increment–Velocity; Product Backlog–Burndown
pool.explanation: The 2020 Scrum Guide pairs each artifact with a commitment as in the first option.

pool.question: A Kanban team has average WIP of 20 items and throughput of 5 items per week. What average cycle time does Little's Law imply?
pool.explanation: Cycle time = WIP / throughput = 20 / 5 = 4 weeks.

pool.question: A manager uses the Daily Scrum to collect status from each developer and assign tasks. What is wrong?
options: Only the Product Owner should speak
The Daily Scrum is for Developers to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt their own plan
pool.explanation: Turning the Daily Scrum into a status meeting undermines self-management and its purpose.

pool.question: Which practice is most central to Kanban?
pool.explanation: WIP limits drive flow; the others are Scrum-related practices.

pool.question: Which practices help hybrid projects succeed? (Select all that apply.)
options: Translating release forecasts into milestone confidence
Shared milestones across agile and predictive components
One integrated risk and dependency log
Separate, conflicting status definitions per team
pool.explanation: Shared milestones, integrated logs and translated forecasts create coherence; conflicting definitions create confusion.

pool.question: Five teams build one product and are frequently blocked by each other. What is the best first step?
options: Add a sixth team to coordinate
Ask teams to work independently without coordination
Visualise cross-team dependencies, plan jointly and redesign teams or architecture to reduce them
Adopt the largest scaling framework immediately
pool.explanation: Address the real coordination problem with the lightest effective structure.

pool.question: A stakeholder has high power and high interest. Which strategy fits?
pool.explanation: High-power, high-interest stakeholders can shape or block the project, so they need close, active engagement.

pool.question: Senior doctors resist a new records system, fearing slower consultations. Which approach is most likely to succeed?
options: Involve them in design and pilots, share data openly and adjust rollout
pool.explanation: Involvement and evidence build ownership among high-power stakeholders.

pool.question: Which behaviours build psychological safety? (Select all that apply.)
options: Thanking people who raise problems early
pool.explanation: Modelling fallibility and rewarding candour build safety; public blame destroys it.

pool.question: What stage of team development is characterised by conflict over roles and approach?
pool.explanation: Storming is the stage where differences surface and must be worked through.

pool.question: Your project ends, but billing complaints are rising after go-live. What is the best closure decision?
options: Close the project as successful because milestones were met
Extend hypercare for billing, assign an owner and capture a lesson on go-live readiness criteria
pool.explanation: Closure should confirm operational readiness and hand over outstanding issues with owners.

pool.question: Which lesson is most likely to change future behaviour?
options: UAT slipped 3 weeks because business testers were unavailable; confirm UAT availability at the planning gate (owner: sponsor)
pool.explanation: Specific cause, action and owner make lessons actionable.

pool.question: A distributed team spans Karachi, Dubai and London. Juniors in one location rarely speak in client calls. Which actions help? (Select all that apply.)
options: Only allowing the most senior person to speak
pool.explanation: These practices increase inclusion and surface problems earlier; restricting voice does the opposite.

pool.question: What should happen before an AI-generated meeting summary is published to the project team?
options: It is sent only to the sponsor
The PM verifies it against the discussion and corrects errors
pool.explanation: AI summaries can misattribute actions; human verification is required for medium-tier outputs.

pool.question: An AI tool summarises vendor proposals and consistently favours one bidder whose wording mirrors the criteria. What should the agency do?
options: Use summaries for navigation only, score from the proposals directly and record how AI was used
pool.explanation: Procurement fairness requires evaluators to judge the source material and document AI use.

pool.question: Which should be included when a project delivers a customer-facing AI feature? (Select all that apply.)
pool.explanation: AI features need specific testing, oversight and monitoring, and documentation of purpose and limits.

pool.question: Which use of AI should be prohibited in project delivery?
options: Drafting a status report for review
Generating test cases from requirements for QA review
Summarising lessons learned for the PMO
Automated decisions on team members' performance ratings without a human decision-maker
pool.explanation: Automated decisions about people carry legal and ethical risks and must remain human decisions.

pool.question: What is the best measure of whether an AI-assisted reporting pilot adds value?
options: Time saved and errors caught, compared with the pre-pilot baseline
pool.explanation: Value measures compare outcomes before and after, not activity.

pool.question: Why do strong PM fundamentals matter more in the AI era?
options: Fundamentals are needed only for exams
Leaders must be able to recognise when AI output is wrong
pool.explanation: Verification and judgment require understanding the underlying methods.

pool.question: A training slide describes the PMBOK Guide as "eight performance domains and twelve principles". What is the most accurate correction for the current (8th) edition?
options: Six principles and seven performance domains, with five focus areas containing 40 processes
Seven principles, seven practices and seven processes
Five process groups and ten knowledge areas only
pool.explanation: The 8th edition (November 2025) has six principles and seven performance domains plus five focus areas. Twelve principles and eight domains describe the 7th edition; seven practices describes PRINCE2 7.

pool.question: A regional insurer's PMO wants an organisation-wide policy that auditors and procurement teams recognise, while its app teams use Scrum. Which combination is most coherent?
options: Replace Scrum with a detailed PRINCE2 process for the app teams
An ISO 21502-aligned policy, board-level tolerances and stage boundaries, Scrum for app delivery, and a tailoring statement explaining the choices
Adopt every framework in full simultaneously
Avoid all standards to stay flexible
pool.explanation: Frameworks do different jobs and can be combined deliberately. A tailoring statement records why each choice fits.

pool.question: Five uncertain tasks have most-likely durations summing to 60 days. A Monte Carlo on their three-point estimates shows a 4% chance of finishing within 60 days and a P80 of 79 days. What should the PM present?
options: 60 days, because it is the sum of the most likely values
A range (for example P50 about 72, P80 about 79 days), the main uncertainties and a proposed commitment
No date until all uncertainty is removed
pool.explanation: Summing most-likely values ignores skew. Present a range with confidence levels and the drivers, then agree a commitment.

pool.question: A burnup shows the team completing about 18 points a week, but total scope has grown by about 15 points a week for two months. What is the most important message to the board?
options: At current net throughput the project will not finish without a scope decision; options are to freeze or descope, add capacity, or move the date
The burnup is wrong because velocity is stable
Report green because velocity is on plan
pool.explanation: Net throughput (completion minus scope growth) is only about 3 points a week. Without a scope decision, the finish recedes regardless of team speed.

pool.question: A team with 30 items in progress finishes 10 per week. It caps WIP at 15 and throughput stays at 10 per week. By Little's Law, what happens to average cycle time?
options: It falls from about 3 weeks to about 1.5 weeks
pool.explanation: Average cycle time ≈ WIP ÷ throughput: 30/10 = 3 weeks before, 15/10 = 1.5 weeks after.

pool.question: A PM builds a weekly AI-assisted status report from Jira data. Which practices are appropriate? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Compute metrics in a script and give the AI only the aggregated status table
Store the Jira API token in an environment variable
Require the AI to cite the table column for every number
Paste raw tickets with customer details into any public chatbot for speed
Verify every figure and cause before publishing and log the AI use
pool.explanation: Code-computed metrics, secure credentials, citations and human verification with a register entry make the pipeline reliable and compliant. Sharing raw personal data with unapproved tools is not acceptable.

pool.question: During a pilot, an AI claims-triage feature agrees with human reviewers far less often for one customer group. What should the project leader do first?
options: Proceed to rollout because overall accuracy is high
Limit the model's use for affected cases, investigate data and model causes with compliance involved, retest, and record the decision
Remove the group from the monitoring report
Ask the vendor to confirm the model is fair and continue
pool.explanation: Differential performance is a fairness and compliance risk. Limit exposure, investigate, involve specialists, retest and document before proceeding.

pool.question: A retrospective note says "testing was rushed". Which version is a lesson that will change behaviour?
options: "Testing was rushed; be more careful next time"
"Engage infrastructure during planning because test environments took 5 weeks; PMO adds environment requests to the planning checklist by the 30th"
pool.explanation: A useful lesson states a cause and an owned, dated action embedded in a checklist or standard. Generic advice changes nothing.
